title: Fruit salad, fresh or raw, with citrus fruits, no dressing

content.title: About
content.content: The fruit salad is made from a variety of fresh fruits, including citrus (oranges, mandarins, grapefruit), apples, pears, berries and other seasonal fruits. It is served without any dressing, allowing the natural taste and aroma of the fruits to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Citrus fruits are rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system.
Combining different fruits can increase the bioavailability of certain nutrients through enzyme interactions.
Fruit salad is commonly served in the summer season as a refreshing and thirst‑quenching dish.
A salad without dressing retains the natural sweetness of the fruits, adding no extra calories.
The variety of colors and textures makes the dish visually appealing.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Citrus fruits and berries provide high levels of vitamin C, a powerful antioxidant that supports immunity.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fruits such as apples and pears are high in soluble and insoluble fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: Without added dressing the salad is low in calories, making it suitable for weight management.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: Because fruits have a high water content, they help maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids found in berries and citrus protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Citrus allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to citrus fruits, ranging from skin rashes to swelling.

items.title: High acidity
items.content: Large amounts of citrus can increase stomach acidity and cause discomfort for people with gastritis or reflux.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: If the fruits are not organic, they may carry pesticide residues; thorough washing before consumption is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled; you can add mint or a squeeze of lime for extra aroma. It is eaten with a spoon or fork and can also be used as a side dish for fish or chicken.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours to preserve freshness and texture.
